extracted.intended_audience: foundation staff, philanthropic researchers, policy analysts, and minority grantseekers (Hispanic-serving organizations)
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis of foundation grantmaking practices, policies, and grant distribution for support of Hispanic needs and concerns based on a mail survey and Foundation Grants Index data. Includes metrics on grant concentration, foundation procedures, publication/transparency, technical assistance, and support for educational R&D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentration of funding (large vs small grants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure and report how much of total grant dollars are accounted for by a small number of large grants (e.g., '36 grants (or 12% of all grants given for the benefit of Hispanics) account for 72% of the total dollar amount').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report counts and percentages of 'large' grants vs 'small' grants, total dollar amounts for each group, and average amounts for small grants (e.g., 'The average amount given for each of the 226 small grants was $17,214').

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorize grants by field of interest and report dollar distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate total dollars and counts of grants across defined fields (Education, Civil Rights & Legal Services, Research, Community Organization & Development, Health, Social Services, Arts & Humanities, Religion) and report percentages (e.g., 'Education (30%), Civil Rights and Legal Services (25%), Research (12%)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide per-field totals, percentages of total monies, counts of large grants per field, and average grant sizes for the remaining grants in each field (examples and per-field top grants are provided in the report).

rubrics_metrics.name: Define and report 'large' grants threshold and metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish 'large' grants (e.g., grants of $100,000 or above in examples provided) from other grants and report number of large grants, total dollar amount of large grants, and distribution across fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tabulate Large Grants: N and Dollar Amount by area and show average amount for all other grants in the area (Table 12). Use explicit thresholds where available or define your own and be consistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average grant reporting for remaining (small) grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute and report average dollar amounts among the remainder of grants in each field (e.g., 'The other 57 grants in this field accounted for the remaining 17%, the average grant among these amounted to $14,472').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include count of remaining grants, total dollar amount, and resulting average; present both per-field and overall averages for transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey sampling/selection criteria for foundations
rubrics_metrics.description: Select foundations for inclusion in the survey based on explicit criteria: foundations that (1) supported Hispanics and minorities and (2) reported to the 1977-78 Foundation Grants Index (FGI). Exclude foundations supporting only non-Hispanic identified minorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document inclusion/exclusion rules clearly; e.g., manual search of FGI to identify foundations supporting Hispanic needs and those that gave at least one grant to unspecified 'minorities.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification rule when multiple foundation-type boxes checked
rubrics_metrics.description: If a foundation marks more than one type (e.g., general purpose and family), decide category using (1) number of donor's family members on the Board and senior staff and (2) range of giving. A foundation with a broad range of giving but more than 40% family members on Board/senior staff is classified as a family foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply an explicit tie-breaker algorithm for coding foundation type and record the decision rules for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-time administrative staff as capacity metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess foundations by whether they employ full-time administrative staff: 'Without professional staff, proposals are not likely to be adequately investigated; applicants will not receive responsive attention... Foundations without staff investigate proposals properly only if a board member has the time and inclination to do so.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report proportion of foundations with full-time staff and analyze relationship to programmatic responsiveness and innovation (the report notes staffed foundations more likely to have innovative/independent programs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and transparency practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure foundation transparency by whether they publish annual/biennial reports, other publications, and by whether tax returns/financials are publicly available (tax returns available at the Foundation Center; private foundations must permit inspection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report N and % issuing annual/biennial reports by asset size and foundation type, and note when foundations provide other publications on policies, grants, and application procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination and responsiveness to inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether foundations will include organizations in mailing lists upon request and whether they will respond to letters of inquiry from prospective applicants (e.g., 'Will Include organizations and institutions in their mailing list, upon request' and 'Will respond to letters of Inquiry' with percentages reported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report percentages and interpret atypical vs typical responsiveness; link dissemination behavior to applicants' ability to identify funding sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of applicant procedural information
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess which types of procedural information foundations will provide to applicants upon request, including application deadlines; suggestions for proposal length; suggestions for proposal format; dates when the Executive Board meets to consider proposals; feedback on preliminary drafts or concept papers; and advice on other funding sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tabulate counts/percentages for each information type (Table 20) and use as metric of accessibility of application process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application processing practices and feedback to applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether foundations acknowledge receipt of proposals, inform unsuccessful applicants in writing, explain reasons for rejection, and advise unsuccessful applicants on alternate funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report proportions performing each action (e.g., 88% would acknowledge receipt; 82% would explain reasons for rejection; only 34% would advise on alternate funding) and discuss implications for applicant learning and capacity-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical assistance availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the availability of technical assistance (TA) to applicants, including whether the foundation has a person who provides TA and whether foundations would contact applicants for additional information, offer technical assistance, encourage revision, or simply reject poorly drafted proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the percent with TA staff (e.g., 24.5% claimed to have a person providing TA) and tabulate likely actions in response to worthy ideas in poorly drafted proposals (Table 21). Discuss the typical lack of TA and its effect on minority organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested improvements for minority applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect and report foundation-suggested ways minority groups could improve funding records: study guidelines and adhere to them; improve quality of proposal contents and structure; improve management, budgeting, and fund-raising capabilities; conduct research on target foundations; request technical assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use frequency counts (e.g., N of foundations making each suggestion) to prioritize capacity-building interventions (Table 22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational definition / components of Educational Research & Development (R&D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define 'Educational Research and Development' operationally by listing constituent activities that foundations may support: internships, graduate fellowships, postdoctoral fellowships, national/regional/state conferences, surveys, community educational needs assessments, ongoing research by organizations and individuals, publication of educational research results, short-term seminars/workshops on research skills, and other specified activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When surveying foundation support, present a checklist of activities (as done in the questionnaire) so foundations can indicate which R&D activities they support; report counts/percentages for each activity (Table 23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance of dedicated Hispanic mailing lists / outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Track whether foundations maintain Hispanic-specific mailing lists, include Hispanics on general mailing lists, or have no mailing list—used as a metric of targeted outreach (e.g., 'Only 11 (10.8%) of the responding foundations indicated that they have an Hispanic mailing list').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report counts/percentages and note alternative dissemination practices (general list inclusion vs none) as indicators of proactive outreach to Hispanic organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure foundation support for Hispanic educational R&D over time
rubrics_metrics.description: Report current and past-five-year support for specific Hispanic educational R&D activities (counts and percentages for each activity category; e.g., internships, fellowships, conferences, surveys, needs assessments, research by organizations/individuals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare 'currently supporting' vs 'over the past five years' to detect trends and declines; present N and (%) for each activity (Table 24).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board composition diversity metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure presence and number of persons of Hispanic origin on foundation boards/trustees as a diversity metric (e.g., 12 foundations claimed Hispanic directors or trustees, representing 13 Hispanic board members).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disaggregate by Hispanic ethnicity (Mexican American, Puerto Rican, Colombian, etc.) and report counts; interpret relative underrepresentation against benchmarks or narrative evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmative action and minority employment indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess foundation employment/equity practices via existence of written affirmative action policies, counts of minority professionals among staff, and counts of minority trustees as indicators of hiring and governance diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report raw counts and percentages (e.g., ABFE findings cited: 64 black professionals among 681 professional personnel, 40 minority trustees among 490) and note rarity of formal written policies as a separate measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey methodology and response-rate reporting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Document survey implementation details (mailing date, follow-up procedures, response rate, confidentiality/verification of answers): e.g., 'A total of 140 foundations were mailed questionnaires on March 12, 1980... A total of 102 questionnaires (73% response rate) were finally received. Questionnaire answers were not externally verified, in an effort to protect confidentiality of respondents.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report response rate by state and other strata (Table 13), describe follow-up procedures, and disclose whether responses were externally verified to allow readers to assess reliability.
